CheckTitle: Workload Identity Federation providers enforce an attribute condition
Description: **Workload Identity Federation providers** define an `attributeCondition` (CEL) that restricts which external identities may impersonate Google Cloud principals. A provider without one trusts every identity issued by the configured OIDC issuer, AWS account, or SAML IdP.
Risk: A workload identity pool provider without an attribute condition accepts any external identity from its issuer. An attacker who can add or edit a provider can trust an identity they control and mint fresh short-lived Google Cloud credentials indefinitely. Because no key is stored, this keyless backdoor survives the credential rotation that standard incident response relies on.

Code.CLI: gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers update-<oidc|aws|saml|x509> <PROVIDER_ID> --location=global --workload-identity-pool=<POOL_ID> --attribute-condition="<CEL_condition>"   # use the update subcommand matching the provider type
Code.Other:
1. In the Google Cloud console, go to IAM & Admin > Workload Identity Federation
2. Open the affected pool and provider
3. Set an attribute condition (CEL) restricting the allowed external identities, using an assertion that fits the provider type: OIDC/SAML by subject or claim (assertion.sub), AWS by account/role (assertion.account), X.509 by certificate subject
4. For OIDC providers, also restrict allowedAudiences to your own audience
5. Review providers regularly for entries you did not create

Recommendation.Text: Set an attribute condition on every active Workload Identity Federation provider so only the intended external identities can impersonate Google Cloud principals, and pair OIDC providers with a restricted audience. Audit pools and providers regularly for unexpected entries.

Notes: Disabled or non-ACTIVE providers cannot vend credentials and are reported as PASS. This check verifies that an attribute condition is present; it does not evaluate whether the condition's expression is sufficiently restrictive.
